Albert -- an emulator for the Tatung Einstein TC-01 (Z80, 1984)
================================================================

Run albert.exe. That is the whole installation.


What is in here
---------------

  albert.exe            the emulator
  SDL3.dll              window, input and audio; must stay beside the exe
  roms\                 the firmware, and the commented sources the
                        debugger reads

If the roms folder is empty, Albert will start but has no machine to be: it
needs an Einstein MOS ROM -- the 8 KB MOS 1.2 image is the one everything here
is written against.

Put one in roms\ and it will be found. Call it einstein.rom and it is loaded
first; failing that, any file in there ending .rom is checked and the first one
that really is an Einstein ROM is used. The name does not matter, because the
contents are hashed to identify it. You can also pass a path on the command
line, or use File > Open.

Nothing else is required. There is no installer, no registry use, and no
Visual C++ runtime to install -- the C runtime is linked in.


Getting something running
-------------------------

  albert.exe --disk mygame.dsk

Some discs boot straight into the game. Others boot XtalDOS to a "0:" prompt,
where you type the program's name -- DIR will list what is on the disc.

To insert a disc while running, use Media > Drive 0 > Insert, or just drop
the file on the window.


Keys
----

  Caps Lock   ALPHA          Pause   BREAK
  Alt         GRAPH          Ctrl    CONTROL

To boot a disc you put in after starting, use Machine > Boot disc. A disc that
was already in the drive when Albert started boots on its own.

Ctrl+Pause, which is what a real Einstein wants, does not work on Windows and
cannot be made to: holding Ctrl turns Pause into a different key, and the
keystroke never reaches the program at all. Ctrl+End does the same job.

  F9    run / pause
  F11   full screen
  F12   show or hide the debugger

The menu is mouse-driven and Alt does not open it. That is forced rather than
chosen: Alt is the Einstein's GRAPH key, and the arrows, Enter, Space and
Escape are all keys on its keyboard, so they belong to the machine.


Joysticks
---------

Options > Joysticks. Joystick 1 defaults to the numeric keypad -- the one part
of the host keyboard the Einstein's own keyboard does not use, so it costs the
machine no keys.

Two joystick interfaces exist and software uses one or the other, so Albert
drives both at once: the analogue sticks read through the ADC, and a digital
stick on the PIO. You should not have to care which a game wants.


Settings
--------

albert.cfg and albert-layout-v3.ini are written next to the executable on
first run. Delete them to go back to defaults.


ROMs and disc images
--------------------

The Einstein firmware is Tatung's copyright, and commercial disc images belong
to their publishers. Whatever is in roms\ here was put there by whoever built
this copy; the emulator itself is separate from it.

The commented disassembly of MOS 1.2 in roms\disassembled is Ric Hohne's work
(1986-87). It is what lets the debugger single-step against named, annotated
source instead of raw mnemonics, and it is the reason this emulator could be
written at all.
